inputs.question: Yusuf Adeyemi, principal data engineer at Wren Valley Health, has ten minutes and no slides to explain differential privacy to a board of trustees on 20 November; half the room is clinicians and donors with no technical background. What I need is not a tutorial but material that is both properly sourced and usable in front of that room. Look for documented instances of an identifiable public institution, statistical agency or regulator publishing figures under a differential-privacy or comparable formal-privacy method — who, when, what they published, and what they said publicly about the trade-off between accuracy and disclosure protection — and for any published guidance or regulatory text bearing on the release of deliberately noised statistics. For each item, give one plain sentence saying what a trustee with no technical background would take from it, and state explicitly what the source does not establish, because the board's question will be 'so are the numbers wrong?' and an overclaim there is worse than a gap. Where the only available material is technical, say so rather than paraphrasing a paper into something it does not say. No breach-rate, re-identification-rate or data-incident statistics: none was asked for and the board will hear one as a threat.
